3.translation: Use four chord backbones and one observed alignment. Map the ribbon fill to the query ID and assign that category one named colour. Sequence colours retain their default scale.

6.translation: | Role | Mapped data | Useful scale family |

13.translation: ## Fixed styles and user scale priority ⟦shared:0⟧

14.translation:
Put a constant style outside ⟦shared:0⟧. Map variable styles inside it and supply an
appropriate scale. An explicitly fixed geom value takes precedence; omitting that
argument keeps mapping active. Your scale takes priority over automatic defaults.
Repeated same-kind layers keep independent data/mapping/parameters. A geometric
vector named by ⟦shared:1⟧ does not mean a scale also accepts per-sequence lists.

16.translation:
⟦shared:0⟧ controls discrete role legends; ⟦shared:1⟧
controls continuous colour guides. The colour/color spelling aliases are retained,
with ⟦shared:2⟧ preferred in this documentation. Use ⟦shared:3⟧ on a layer,
⟦shared:4⟧ for guide choices and ⟦shared:5⟧ for placement.
A wide guide may need multiple rows or a wider export, not smaller biological data.

17.translation: ## Select a theme for the scene ⟦shared:0⟧

18.translation: This page uses the default theme. Add ⟦shared:0⟧ to adjust text, legends or background; for example, ⟦shared:1⟧ sets the base text size. ⟦shared:2⟧ provides a publication style and ⟦shared:3⟧ suits circular maps. Themes control non-data appearance without changing coordinates or mapped colours.

20.translation:
Add ⟦shared:0⟧ to opt into target-size layout. The bundled example uses
recorded sequence lengths and HSPs; the reference canvas is in inches and the
automatic text floor is in mm. The report describes the requested 8 × 6 inch
PNG; use the same size with standard ⟦shared:1⟧ to reproduce that arrangement.

22.translation:
⟦shared:0⟧ holds default theme and guide furniture at reference physical sizes.
⟦shared:1⟧ adjusts theme-driven defaults within the chosen multiplier range.
⟦shared:2⟧ adds a bounded joint search for native guide grids, sides and
directions, then remeasures the result. It reuses existing label layout;
⟦shared:3⟧ is a guide-space result, not a promise that every label is collision-free.
No policy preserves the existing plotting behaviour.

23.translation:
Explicit geom styles, theme sizes, guide positions/directions/grids/key sizes,
scales and ⟦shared:0⟧ remain authoritative. Continuous/stepped bars remain
intact; categories and source records are retained. When constraints exceed the
canvas budget, diagnostics report ⟦shared:1⟧ and rendering warns.
Increase the export size or revise the explicit guide settings. The bounded
search does not guarantee a global optimum. Layout-only exports record the
policy but require a target device for final guide measurements.

24.translation:
Apply the policy to each desired Fusion panel before composing it. Each panel
uses its allocated size; outer panel allocations and the cross-panel guide are
separate. Facets, arbitrary custom grobs, blanket scaling of geometric constants
and font embedding certification are outside this policy.

26.translation: Links from the same query share a colour; continuous identity needs a continuous scale. Put fixed colours outside aes() and make each guide explain its mapping.

28.translation: See [scale families](⟦shared:0⟧) for runnable manual/continuous/steps/identity, line type, opacity and theme examples.

29.translation: ## Detailed appearance with standard theme syntax ⟦shared:0⟧

30.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧ already supplies ⟦shared:1⟧. Choose one of the four presets only when its appearance suits the figure: Minimal reduces decoration; Publication uses compact typography; Dark changes non-data decoration for a dark background; Plasmid emphasises circular annotations. Palettes, scientific relationships and sequence directions remain independent. Use explicit data scales or fixed geom colours when a background requires different data contrast.

34.translation: | Sequence colours, feature fill, numerical Track range/breaks/units | ⟦shared:0⟧ and the corresponding scale |

35.translation: | Backbone form, Ribbon arrow/gradient mode, fixed data styles | Geom |

36.translation: | Track band, feature stacking and offsets | Position |

37.translation: | Sequence order/direction and projection | Coord / explicit data workflow |

38.translation: | Guide rows, columns, order, direction and individual position | Guide; global placement in theme |

39.translation: The registered ⟦shared:0⟧ physical settings accept scalar absolute units, just like the existing short arguments in ⟦shared:1⟧. Prefer ⟦shared:2⟧ for later adjustments. Use one spelling in a theme constructor; supplying both spellings for the same setting is an error. A later ⟦shared:3⟧ merges fields in the familiar ggplot2 order. ⟦shared:4⟧, ⟦shared:5⟧, ⟦shared:6⟧ and their ⟦shared:7⟧ line elements style their actual annotation layers, while explicit geom styles/mappings remain authoritative. Ordinary Cartesian ⟦shared:8⟧ is not a substitute for the automatic genomic sequence axis; Dotplot has independent native x/y axes.

40.translation: ### Shared Track appearance and local overrides ⟦shared:0⟧

41.translation: The following real GC fractions come from the unchanged bundled pUC19 sequence. It needs optional dplyr. The Track's data scale owns the fraction domain and unit; its local native Guide owns axis appearance. The ordinary theme owns shared decorations. No coverage or read support is invented.

43.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧ control shared numerical-axis styles; ⟦shared:1⟧ and ⟦shared:2⟧ are nonnegative absolute units. Resolved font/family/angle metrics are used when reserving plot space. The GC Guide's explicit text style wins over the later shared 9pt default. A local ⟦shared:3⟧ hides just that decoration. ⟦shared:4⟧ supports local ⟦shared:5⟧, ⟦shared:6⟧ and ⟦shared:7⟧; other options fail explicitly instead of being silently ignored.

44.translation: Layers with one Track ID share a band, value domain and one numerical reference; distinct IDs already have independent value/fill/colour scales and colour guides. Add ⟦shared:0⟧ for each ID rather than a theme element named after every track. Colour-guide appearance can use the native ⟦shared:1⟧ or ⟦shared:2⟧ supplied to the corresponding Track colour scale. Global legend fonts/background/placement remain theme concerns. Sequence order, HSP selection, statistics and units never change when switching themes. Automatic label/Guide layout is a separate policy and remeasures at the final export size.

45.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧⟦shared:1⟧Put common adjustments in the appropriate ggplot2 component: mappings, geometry, positions, coordinates and themes have distinct roles.⟦shared:2⟧⟦shared:3⟧

48.translation: [Plotting concepts](⟦shared:0⟧) explains layers, mappings, scales and coordinates. The example below applies that distinction to alignment identity.

53.translation:
Use ⟦shared:0⟧ for signed strand offsets.
⟦shared:1⟧ handles overlapping features; ⟦shared:2⟧
allocates a named quantitative lane. Geometric sequence parameters accept one
value, a matching unnamed vector, or a vector named by ⟦shared:3⟧; named vectors
are recommended. This syntax does not extend to scales, guides or themes.

54.translation:
Each layer owns its own ⟦shared:0⟧, ⟦shared:1⟧ and parameters. Repeated feature or
link layers do not replace one another. Use ordinary ggplot2 ⟦shared:2⟧ and
⟦shared:3⟧; role input mappings precede geometry, while staged visual mappings
follow ggplot2 evaluation. See the [API contract](⟦shared:4⟧).

56.translation: Use a coordinate for global rotation, named values for per-sequence geometry, and mappings plus scales for data-dependent colour.
